items.titleJa: {魚|さかな}と{風|かぜ}と、わたしだけの{日記|にっき}
items.titleEn: Fish, Wind, and a Diary Just for Me

items.recapEn: At Numazu's five o'clock fish market Hana saw fish she could not name and horse mackerel drying in the wind; Ōno-san said salt and wind make them delicious. Ken bought three for breakfast. Then Hana wrote her diary in plain form for the first time: walking is fun, her feet hurt, Ken cooks well. Tomorrow, Fuji, probably.

items.recapEn: At Ōno-san's stall Ken picked out horse mackerel and asked the price: four hundred yen each, three for a thousand. Hana thought that expensive; Ken did not, and bought three. At breakfast he cooked them, just salt and wind, and Hana praised him. He noticed her diary had no desu today and said he thought that was good.

items.recapEn: Hana posted on a walking forum from Numazu, town twelve: up at five, the fish market by the sea, fish she could not name, and horse mackerel with nothing but salt and wind, the best fish so far, she thinks. Four hundred yen each; not expensive after all. Fuji still unseen; tomorrow, Hara.
